questions.explanation: Use 'this' for one near thing.
questions.q: ___ is my pen. (near me, one pen)

questions.explanation: Use 'that' for one far thing.
questions.q: ___ is your book over there. (far, one book)

questions.explanation: Use 'these' for many near things.
Use 'those' for many far things.
questions.q: ___ are his keys over there. (far, many keys)

questions.explanation: Use 'these' with a plural noun for near things.
Use 'that' with a singular noun for a far thing.
questions.q: Look at ___ bird in the tree. (far, one bird)

questions.explanation: Use 'this' for one near person.
Use 'those' with a plural noun for far things.
Use 'this' for one near thing in a question.
Use 'that' to talk about one thing in the past.
questions.q: ___ was a great day! (past, one day)

questions.explanation: Use 'these' with a plural noun for near things.
questions.q: Come and see ___ photos. (near, many photos)

questions.explanation: Use 'those' with a plural noun for far people.
Use 'that' for one far thing.
Use 'these' with a plural noun for near things.
Use 'these are' with a plural noun for near people.
Use 'this is' with a singular noun for a near thing.
'Those is his shoes' is wrong because 'those' needs 'are' with a plural noun.
Use 'that' with 'is' for one far thing.
Use 'these' with 'are' for many near things.
Use 'these are' with a plural noun for near people.
